# Book components

<!-- Generated by `just catalog` from components/book/catalog.ts. Edit that file, not this one. -->

Everything a chapter's MDX can use, without imports. Live demos: `/components` on the dev site (`just run`).

- Diagrams show **facts from the spec or precomputed data**, never the code a section asks the reader to write.
- Every diagram takes an optional `caption`; cite its source there when it reproduces a spec or datasheet.
- `highlight` marks the one thing the text is talking about. Use it sparingly.
- Math is plain MDX: `$inline$` and `$$ display $$`, typeset by KaTeX.

## Writing

### Idea

The one idea a section rests on, said once and large.

- children: the idea, one or two sentences

```mdx
<Idea>
  A layer only talks to the layers right above and below it.
</Idea>
```

### Aside

A side remark. type is note (default), tip or warning; title is optional.

- type?: 'note' | 'tip' | 'warning' (default note)
- title?: string
- children

```mdx
<Aside type="warning" title="Byte order">
  Multi-byte fields go over the wire **big-endian**, whatever your CPU uses.
</Aside>
```

### Cite

An inline pointer to the source of a claim.

- href: URL of the source
- children: the source, e.g. "RFC 791 §3.1"

```mdx
Every IPv4 header starts with its version <Cite href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791#section-3.1">RFC 791 §3.1</Cite>.
```

### Term

A word with its definition on hover or keyboard focus.

- def: the definition
- children: the word

```mdx
Each hop lowers the <Term def="Time to Live: how many more routers may pass the packet on.">TTL</Term> by one.
```

### Check

A self-check: answer it in your head, then open the answer, written on the paper underneath.

- question
- children: the answer

```mdx
<Check question="Two hosts on the same switch: does a frame between them pass through your router?">
  No. The switch forwards it by MAC address, straight from one port to the other.
</Check>
```

### Figure

An image (src, alt) or any diagram as children, with a caption.

- src?: image path
- alt?
- caption?
- children?: any diagram instead of src

```mdx
<Figure src="/diagrams/layers.svg" alt="The four layers" caption="Each layer wraps the one above it." />
```

### Kbd

A key to press.

- children: the key

```mdx
Stop the capture with <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>C</Kbd>.
```

## Section structure

### Task

What to build next, in prose. Holds the Spec entries for the section.

- title? (default "What to build")
- children: prose and <Spec name kind?> entries

```mdx
<Task>
  Write a word counter. It works on any text, including empty text.

  <Spec name="Count" kind="function">
    Takes a string and returns how many words it holds. A word is a run
    of characters between whitespace. Never fails.
  </Spec>
  <Spec name="ErrTooLong" kind="error">
    Reported by `CountFile` when a line is over 64 KiB.
  </Spec>
</Task>
```

### Hints

Tiered hints, revealed one at a time, smallest nudge first.

- children: <Hint> entries, smallest nudge first

```mdx
<Hints>
  <Hint>What does your counter do with two spaces in a row?</Hint>
  <Hint>Count the starts of words, not the spaces between them.</Hint>
  <Hint>A word starts where a non-space follows a space, or at the very beginning.</Hint>
</Hints>
```

### Terminal

A command and what it prints. ok/PASS lines turn green, FAIL/panic lines amber.

- command
- output?: what it prints
- title?

```mdx
<Terminal
  title="Run the tests"
  command="go test ./count"
  output={`--- FAIL: TestCount/two_spaces (0.00s)
    count_test.go:21: Count("a  b") = 3, want 2
FAIL
FAIL	example/count	0.003s`}
/>
```

### DoneWhen

The checks that say a section is finished. Ticks are remembered in the reader's browser.

- items: string[]
- title? (default "You're done when")

```mdx
<DoneWhen
  items={[
    'go test ./count passes',
    'Your count of Moby-Dick matches wc -w',
    'Empty input gives 0, not an error',
  ]}
/>
```

### ShowOff

The moment the code meets the real world. The book's paper at full strength; the loudest block in a chapter.

- title? (default "Show it off")
- children

```mdx
<ShowOff title="Count a real book">
  Download *Moby-Dick* from Project Gutenberg and count it. Compare with `wc -w`.
</ShowOff>
```

### Recap

What the reader has now, at the end of a chapter. Write a Markdown list inside; every line gets a tick.

- title? (default "What you have now")
- children: a Markdown list

```mdx
<Recap>
  - A word counter that handles any whitespace
  - Line and byte counts
  - Tests that pin it all down
</Recap>
```

### Reference

The chapter's reference implementation, folded away. title and note are optional.

- title?
- note?
- children: a code block

```mdx
<Reference>
  ```go
  ...
  ```
</Reference>
```

### Challenge

An optional extra: something to build with what you know now. A dashed outline, a sketch to fill in.

- title
- children

```mdx
<Challenge title="Count lines too">
  Make your counter report lines and bytes as well, like `wc`.
  Then make it read from standard input when no file is given.
</Challenge>
```

### Deepening

An optional extra: a way to dig further into how the real thing does it. Finer paper, with more sheets underneath.

- title
- children

```mdx
<Deepening title="What is a word, really?">
  Unicode defines word boundaries in UAX #29. Read it, and find three
  inputs where your counter and the standard disagree.
</Deepening>
```

## Bytes and protocols

### Bitfield

A header laid out bit by bit, RFC style. width defaults to 32; bits can be "variable"; highlight marks the field the text is about.

- fields: { name, bits: number | 'variable', highlight? }[]
- width? (default 32)
- caption?

```mdx
<Bitfield
  caption="The IPv4 header (RFC 791, section 3.1)."
  fields={[
    { name: 'Version', bits: 4 },
    { name: 'IHL', bits: 4 },
    ...
    { name: 'Time to Live', bits: 8, highlight: true },
    ...
    { name: 'Options', bits: 'variable' },
  ]}
/>
```

### HexDump

Bytes as a hex dump with labelled ranges. Point at a byte or a label to pick out its range.

- bytes: hex string, whitespace ignored
- ranges?: { start, length, label }[]
- columns? (default 16)

```mdx
<HexDump
  bytes="ff ff ff ff ff ff  02 00 00 00 00 01  08 06  00 01 08 00 06 04 00 01"
  ranges={[
    { start: 0, length: 6, label: 'Destination' },
    { start: 6, length: 6, label: 'Source' },
    { start: 12, length: 2, label: 'EtherType' },
  ]}
/>
```

### Ladder

Who sends what to whom, time running down. lost draws a message that never arrives.

- parties: string[]
- messages: { from, to, label, note?, lost? }[]
- caption?

```mdx
<Ladder
  parties={['Client', 'Server']}
  messages={[
    { from: 'Client', to: 'Server', label: 'SYN', note: 'seq=100' },
    { from: 'Server', to: 'Client', label: 'SYN, ACK', note: 'seq=300 ack=101' },
    { from: 'Client', to: 'Server', label: 'ACK', lost: true },
    { from: 'Server', to: 'Client', label: 'SYN, ACK', note: 'again, after a timeout' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Learning a language

### CodeCompare

The same thing in two or three languages side by side, for learning a new language from one you know. Children are fenced code blocks with titles.

- children: fenced code blocks, each with title="Language"
- caption?

```mdx
<CodeCompare>

```py title="Python"
nums = [3, 1, 4]
total = 0
for n in nums:
    total += n
```

```go title="Go"
nums := []int{3, 1, 4}
total := 0
for _, n := range nums {
	total += n
}
```

</CodeCompare>
```

### Predict

"What does this print?": code to read, a moment to guess, then the real output and why. For the surprising corners of a language.

- children: a fenced code block
- output: what it really prints
- why?: the explanation
- question? (default "What does this print?")

```mdx
<Predict output="3 3.5" why="Both operands of 7 / 2 are untyped integer constants, so / divides integers. 7.0 is a float constant.">

```go
fmt.Println(7/2, 7.0/2)
```

</Predict>
```

### CodeNotes

A code block with numbered notes on its lines. Pointing at a note lights up the lines it explains.

- children: a fenced code block
- notes: { line: number | [from, to], text }[] (lines count from 1)

```mdx
<CodeNotes
  notes={[
    { line: 1, text: 'Every Go file starts by naming its package; main makes a program.' },
    { line: 3, text: 'Imports are by path. fmt formats and prints.' },
    { line: [5, 7], text: 'main is where the program starts.' },
  ]}
>

```go
package main
...
```

</CodeNotes>
```

### Trace

Steps through a program line by line: the current line lit, every variable and its value, and the output so far. Values that just changed stand out.

- children: a fenced code block
- steps: { line, vars?: { name: value }, out?: printed text, note? }[]

```mdx
<Trace
  steps={[
    { line: 1, vars: { total: '0' } },
    { line: 2, vars: { total: '0', i: '1' } },
    { line: 3, vars: { total: '1', i: '1' } },
    { line: 4, vars: { total: '1', i: '1' }, out: '1\n' },
    ...
  ]}
>

```go
total := 0
for i := 1; i <= 3; i++ {
	total += i
	fmt.Println(total)
}
```

</Trace>
```

### Diagnostic

A compiler error or warning drawn the way rustc prints them: message, location, source lines with the problem marked, and help. For learning to read errors.

- level?: 'error' | 'warning' | 'note'
- code?: e.g. "E0382"
- message
- file?: e.g. "src/main.rs:4:20"
- source: the source lines
- firstLine? (default 1)
- labels?: { line, col, len?, text?, primary? }[]
- notes?: string[], e.g. "help: …"

```mdx
<Diagnostic
  code="E0382"
  message="borrow of moved value: `s`"
  file="src/main.rs:4:20"
  firstLine={2}
  source={`    let s = String::from("hi");
    let t = s;
    println!("{}", s);`}
  labels={[
    { line: 3, col: 13, text: 'value moved here' },
    { line: 4, col: 20, primary: true, text: 'value borrowed here after move' },
  ]}
  notes={['help: consider cloning the value if the performance cost is acceptable']}
/>
```

### Memory

Stack and heap: frames with their variables, heap blocks, an arrow from each pointer to what it points at. For ownership, references, slices.

- stack: { name, vars: { name, value?, to?: heap id, highlight? }[] }[] (innermost first)
- heap?: { id, label?, cells: string[], freed?, highlight? }[]
- caption?

```mdx
<Memory
  stack={[{ name: 'main', vars: [
    { name: 's', value: '(moved)' },
    { name: 't', to: 'buf', highlight: true },
  ] }]}
  heap={[{ id: 'buf', label: 'String data', cells: ['h', 'i'] }]}
/>
```

### Quiz

A multiple-choice question with an explanation for every option. Picking one reveals if it is right and why.

- question
- options: { text, correct?, why? }[]
- children?: e.g. a code block between question and options

```mdx
<Quiz
  question="What is the zero value of a string in Go?"
  options={[
    { text: '""', correct: true, why: 'Every type has a zero value; for strings it is the empty string.' },
    { text: 'nil', why: 'A string is a value, not a pointer, so it can never be nil.' },
  ]}
/>
```

### CodeMarks

Marks inside any fenced code block, no component needed: [!code highlight], [!code ++] and [!code --] for a diff, [!code focus]. Put them in a comment at the end of the line.

- // [!code highlight]
- // [!code ++]  and  // [!code --]
- // [!code focus]
- title="file.go" after the language

```mdx
```go title="main.go"
name := "world"
fmt.Println("hello", name) // [!code --]
fmt.Printf("hello, %s!\n", name) // [!code ++]
```
```

## Compilers and interpreters

### Tokens

A line of source cut into tokens, each with its kind under it. Kinds get a color each; highlight picks tokens by index.

- tokens: [kind, text][]
- source?: the line they came from
- highlight?: number[] (token indices)
- caption?

```mdx
<Tokens
  source="let total = price * 3;"
  tokens={[
    ['keyword', 'let'], ['ident', 'total'], ['op', '='],
    ['ident', 'price'], ['op', '*'], ['number', '3'], ['punct', ';'],
  ]}
  highlight={[4]}
/>
```

### Tree

A tree drawn top-down, written as an S-expression: ASTs, B-trees, scene graphs. A leading ! highlights a node; quote labels with spaces.

- data: S-expression string, e.g. "(+ 1 !(* 2 3))", or { label, children?, highlight? }
- caption?

```mdx
<Tree data='(let total (* price 3))' caption="The tree a parser builds for let total = price * 3." />

<Tree data='(+ 1 !(* 2 3))' />
```

### Grammar

BNF or EBNF rules, one per line. Nonterminals link to their rule, quoted terminals stand out; highlight picks rules by name.

- rules: string, one `name = body ;` (or ::=, →) per line; lines starting with | continue a rule
- highlight?: string[] (rule names)
- id?: anchor prefix, for two grammars on a page
- caption?

```mdx
<Grammar
  highlight={['term']}
  rules={`expr   = term { ("+" | "-") term } ;
term   = factor { ("*" | "/") factor } ;
factor = NUMBER | "(" expr ")" ;`}
/>
```

### Pipeline

Stages in a row and what flows between them. Wraps on narrow screens.

- stages: { name, note?, out?: label on the arrow after it, highlight? }[]
- caption?

```mdx
<Pipeline
  stages={[
    { name: 'Source', out: 'text' },
    { name: 'Lexer', out: 'tokens', highlight: true },
    { name: 'Parser', out: 'AST' },
    { name: 'Compiler', out: 'bytecode' },
    { name: 'VM', note: 'runs it' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Theory

### Derivation

A derivation, one sentential form per line. Brackets mark the symbol rewritten next; rules name the rule used at each step.

- steps: string[], e.g. "[E] + T"
- rules?: string[] (one fewer than steps)
- caption?

```mdx
<Derivation
  steps={['[E]', '[E] + T', '[T] + T', '[F] + T', 'n + [T]', 'n + [F]', 'n + n']}
  rules={['E → E + T', 'E → T', 'T → F', 'F → n', 'T → F', 'F → n']}
/>
```

### StateMachine

States in a row, transitions as arcs: right-going above, left-going below, self-loops on top. initial and accepting for automata.

- states: { id, label?, initial?, accepting?, highlight? }[] (drawn in this order)
- transitions: { from, to, label, highlight? }[]
- caption?

```mdx
<StateMachine
  caption="A DFA for strings over {a, b} that end in ab."
  states={[{ id: 'q0', initial: true }, { id: 'q1' }, { id: 'q2', accepting: true }]}
  transitions={[
    { from: 'q0', to: 'q0', label: 'b' },
    { from: 'q0', to: 'q1', label: 'a' },
    { from: 'q1', to: 'q1', label: 'a' },
    { from: 'q1', to: 'q2', label: 'b', highlight: true },
    { from: 'q2', to: 'q1', label: 'a' },
    { from: 'q2', to: 'q0', label: 'b' },
  ]}
/>
```

### Tape

A Turing machine's tape, the head over one cell with the state on it. One tape, or steps for a run. _ is a blank cell.

- tape?: string, one symbol per character
- head?: cell index
- state?
- steps?: { tape, head, state?, note? }[]
- blank? (default '_')
- caption?

```mdx
<Tape
  steps={[
    { tape: '_101_', head: 1, state: 'q0', note: 'start' },
    { tape: '_101_', head: 2, state: 'q0', note: 'q0, 1 → q0, 1, R' },
    { tape: '_101_', head: 3, state: 'q0', note: 'q0, 0 → q0, 0, R' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Embedded and hardware

### Register

A memory-mapped register as a datasheet draws it: bit numbers counting down, access per field, reset value bit by bit. Fields most significant first.

- name
- address?
- reset?: e.g. "0xA800_0000"
- fields: { name?, bits, access?, reserved?, highlight? }[] (MSB first, must sum to width)
- width? (default 32)
- row? bits per row (default 16)
- caption?

```mdx
<Register
  name="GPIOA_MODER"
  address="0x4002_0000"
  reset="0xA800_0000"
  fields={[
    { name: 'MODER15', bits: 2, access: 'rw' },
    ...
    { name: 'MODER5', bits: 2, access: 'rw', highlight: true },
    ...
    { name: 'MODER0', bits: 2, access: 'rw' },
  ]}
/>
```

### MemoryMap

An address space as stacked regions, high addresses on top. Not to scale; each row shows its range and size. Holes are drawn and labelled.

- regions: { name, start, end (inclusive), note?, highlight? }[]
- digits? hex digits per address (default 8)
- gapLabel? (default 'unmapped')
- caption?

```mdx
<MemoryMap
  digits={4}
  gapLabel="not usable"
  regions={[
    { name: 'ROM bank 00', start: '0x0000', end: '0x3FFF' },
    { name: 'VRAM', start: '0x8000', end: '0x9FFF', highlight: true },
    { name: 'OAM', start: '0xFE00', end: '0xFE9F', note: 'sprite attributes' },
    ...
  ]}
/>
```

### Timing

A digital timing diagram, WaveDrom-style: one character per period. p/n clock, 0/1 level, = data, x unknown, z high-Z, . repeat.

- signals: { name, wave, data?: string[] (labels for = periods), highlight? }[]
- ticks?: string[] (labels under periods)
- caption?

```mdx
<Timing
  ticks={['', '7', '6', '5', '4', '3', '2', '1', '0', '']}
  signals={[
    { name: 'CS', wave: '10.......1' },
    { name: 'SCK', wave: '0p.......0', highlight: true },
    { name: 'MOSI', wave: 'x========x', data: ['1', '0', '1', '0', '0', '1', '1', '0'] },
  ]}
/>
```

### Pinout

A chip or board with labelled pins. pins in package order lay out like a DIP; or give left and right for two headers.

- name?: printed on the chip
- pins?: (string | { name, note?, highlight? })[] in package order
- left?, right?: the same, each top to bottom
- caption?

```mdx
<Pinout
  name="ATmega328P"
  pins={[
    { name: 'PC6', note: 'RESET' }, { name: 'PD0', note: 'RXD' }, { name: 'PD1', note: 'TXD' },
    ...
    { name: 'PB5', note: 'SCK', highlight: true },
    ...
  ]}
/>
```

### RegisterFile

A CPU's registers, one row per group: paired 8-bit registers side by side, 16-bit ones full width.

- rows: { name, bits, value?, note?, highlight? }[][]
- caption?

```mdx
<RegisterFile
  rows={[
    [{ name: 'A', bits: 8, value: '0x01', note: 'accumulator' }, { name: 'F', bits: 8, value: '0xB0', note: 'flags Z N H C' }],
    [{ name: 'B', bits: 8, value: '0x00' }, { name: 'C', bits: 8, value: '0x13' }],
    [{ name: 'SP', bits: 16, value: '0xFFFE' }],
    [{ name: 'PC', bits: 16, value: '0x0100', highlight: true }],
  ]}
/>
```

### OpcodeTable

An instruction set. list: pattern, mnemonic, effect, with operand letters in color (CHIP-8). grid: a 16×16 opcode map colored by group (Game Boy, 6502).

- ops: { code, name, effect?, group?, highlight? }[]
- layout?: 'list' | 'grid' (default list)
- groups?: { key: label } for the grid legend
- caption?

```mdx
<OpcodeTable
  ops={[
    { code: '00E0', name: 'CLS', effect: 'Clear the display.' },
    { code: '6XNN', name: 'LD Vx, NN', effect: 'Vx = NN.' },
    { code: '8XY4', name: 'ADD Vx, Vy', effect: 'Vx = Vx + Vy; VF = carry.', highlight: true },
  ]}
/>

<OpcodeTable layout="grid" groups={{ load: 'Load', alu: 'Arithmetic' }} ops={[{ code: '0x3E', name: 'LD A,n8', group: 'load' }, ...]} />
```

## Graphics and math

### Matrix

A matrix in brackets with optional row and column labels and highlighted cells, rows or columns.

- rows: (string | number)[][]
- name?: written before it, e.g. "T ="
- rowLabels?, columnLabels?: string[]
- highlight?: [row, col][]
- highlightRows?, highlightColumns?: number[]
- caption?

```mdx
<Matrix
  name="T ="
  rows={[[1, 0, 'tx'], [0, 1, 'ty'], [0, 0, 1]]}
  highlightColumns={[2]}
  caption="A 2D translation in homogeneous coordinates."
/>
```

### Plane

A 2D coordinate plane with points, vectors and polygons. yDown flips y for screen and pixel coordinates.

- x?, y?: [min, max] (default [-1, 5])
- step? grid spacing
- yDown?
- points?: { at: [x, y], label?, highlight? }[]
- vectors?: { from?, to, label?, highlight? }[]
- shapes?: { points: [x, y][], label?, closed?, highlight? }[]
- caption?

```mdx
<Plane
  shapes={[{ points: [[0.5, 0.5], [4, 1], [1.5, 4]], label: 'T' }]}
  points={[{ at: [3, 1.6], label: 'P', highlight: true }]}
  vectors={[{ from: [0.5, 0.5], to: [4, 1], label: 'e0' }]}
/>
```

### PixelGrid

A small framebuffer, one character per pixel: . empty, # accent, o second series, + ink, - faint. overlay draws polygons in pixel coordinates.

- pixels: string[] (one string per row)
- palette?: { char: CSS color }
- ruler? (default true)
- centers?: dot every pixel center
- overlay?: { points: [x, y][], label? }[]
- caption?

```mdx
<PixelGrid
  centers
  overlay={[{ points: [[1.2, 6.6], [10.6, 1.4], [7.4, 7.6]] }]}
  pixels={[
    '............',
    '..........#.',
    '.........#..',
    ...
  ]}
/>
```

### Waveform

Signals over time: textbook waves or precomputed samples, as lines or stems. Oscillators, aliasing, filters.

- signals: { wave?: 'sine' | 'square' | 'saw' | 'triangle', freq?, amp?, phase? (cycles), samples?: number[], stems?, label? }[]
- duration? (default 2)
- unit? (default 's')
- caption?

```mdx
<Waveform
  signals={[
    { wave: 'sine', label: 'sine, 1 Hz' },
    { wave: 'sine', freq: 1, stems: true, label: 'sampled at 12 Hz' },
  ]}
/>
```

### Math

Math typeset by KaTeX: $…$ inline, $$…$$ on its own lines. Not a component: plain MDX syntax.

- $inline$
- $$ display $$ (on their own lines)

```mdx
A point is inside when all three edge functions agree in sign, $E_0, E_1, E_2 \ge 0$:

$$
E(P) = (b_x - a_x)(P_y - a_y) - (b_y - a_y)(P_x - a_x)
$$
```

## Media

### Spoiler

Hides an image (or any children) behind a blur and a crossed-out eye until the reader clicks. It can be hidden again.

- src?: image path
- alt?
- label? (default 'Click to reveal')
- caption?
- children?: any content instead of src

```mdx
<Spoiler src="/images/expected-render.png" alt="The triangle, antialiased" label="What your render should look like" />
```

### ImageCompare

Two images of the same size with a bar to slide between them. Drag on the image, or focus it and use the arrow keys.

- before, after: image paths
- beforeLabel?, afterLabel? (default 'Before', 'After')
- alt?
- start? percent (default 50)
- pixelated?: keep pixels crisp
- caption?

```mdx
<ImageCompare
  before="/images/aliased.png"
  after="/images/antialiased.png"
  beforeLabel="1 sample"
  afterLabel="16 samples"
  pixelated
/>
```
